panels.title: Ready
panels.description: The readiness probe is /healthz, which is 503 for as long as the gateway is not connected. 0 means nobody in the guild is getting an answer.

panels.title: Sandboxes live
panels.description: Sandboxes leased to threads. At MATE_MAX_SANDBOXES a turn that needs one takes the sandbox of a thread idle for five minutes, or waits. It counts threads, not Sandboxes, so the warm spare mate keeps beside them is not in it.

panels.title: Threads waiting
panels.description: Threads waiting for a free turn, first in first out. A turn slot frees as soon as a turn ends, so ten minutes above zero is MateThreadsQueued.

panels.title: Turns (rolling day)
panels.description: The same rolling 24h window mate itself counts against MATE_MAX_TURNS_PER_DAY. Past 120 every thread is told the day is spent.

panels.title: Turns per hour, by how they ended
panels.description: end_turn is the model finishing. cancelled is the Stop button. error is a run pi gave up on, usually at the provider; brain-failed is mate losing the thread's session store, or its own agent loop failing. A sandbox that dies mid-turn is a tool error, not an ending.

panels.title: Time to first token
panels.description: From the prompt reaching the model to the first streamed word of the answer — what the human watches an empty message for. A turn that runs a tool before it writes counts the tool, and any sandbox it waits for, in here.

panels.title: Sandbox mints per hour, by result
panels.description: mint-failed is the Sandbox never going Ready; connect-failed is a Ready pod whose mate-hands would not answer, or answered in an older protocol. Either leaves the turn's tool calls failing.

panels.title: Teardowns per hour, by reason
panels.description: quiet and archived are the sandbox being reaped as designed. preempted is an idle thread's sandbox given to a waiting turn. inherited is a sandbox an older mate minted, condemned at boot. restart is a mate that died holding one, and error a sandbox torn down under a failure.

panels.title: How long a sandbox takes to arrive
Time to a Ready sandbox
panels.description: How long the Sandbox takes to go Ready: a kata VM booting, the image landing and a shallow clone finishing, all of it ahead of the first tool call's result. One line per source, and mints are rare enough that most of this panel is gaps.

panels.title: Time to connected hands
panels.description: The rest of the first tool call's wait: the `pods/exec` stream opening, then the mate-hands hello. Paid once per turn that runs a tool, on a reused sandbox too.

panels.title: Warm spares
panels.description: What the last sweep left the pool holding Ready, against MATE_SPARES. Ready below wanted for longer than a sweep or two is a pool that has stopped refilling, and nothing else on this dashboard shows it: threads still get their answers, at the cold start on the panels to the left.

panels.title: Tool calls per hour, by tool and result
panels.description: Each tool call the model made, by tool and whether it returned an error. bash, read, write and edit run in the sandbox through mate-hands; kthx is every bridged kthx_* tool. A climb in errors on one tool is that tool, not the model.

panels.title: Hands call latency p95, by method
panels.description: How long each mate-hands method takes to answer, at the 95th percentile. exec is the command itself and can run for minutes; the file methods are a round trip into the sandbox and should stay well under a second.

panels.title: Turn sandboxes per hour, by source
panels.description: What each turn's tool calls found. none is a chat-only turn, which mints nothing; reused is the thread's own sandbox, spare a warm one adopted, fresh a cold mint, and failed no sandbox at all.

panels.title: Hands links per hour
panels.description: Links opened by result, and links dropped by reason. A turn opens one link on its first tool call; superseded is a connect refused because another live link holds the sandbox at the same or a newer epoch, which mate retries once past, and mismatch an image too old for mate's protocol. closed is the stream ending, unresponsive a daemon that stopped answering pings, and deadline and abort-grace a call that never answered.

panels.title: kthx MCP bridge up
panels.description: 1 while mate holds a listing of the kthx engine's tools and reaches the engine, 0 while it retries. No series means MATE_KTHX_MCP_URL or KTHX_AGENT_TOKEN is unset, and the agent has no kthx tools.

panels.title: Resumes per hour, by result
panels.description: Turns a mate restart cut off. resumed picked up where it stopped, in a fresh message; discarded was aborted, because the thread had no turn in flight or had used its two resumes; lost is a turn mate marked in flight with no open run left to resume, so its answer is gone.

panels.title: Provider errors per hour, by kind
panels.description: Runs that ended in a provider error. auth is the key in Secret mate-opencode, limit the plan's usage cap, timeout a provider that stopped answering, and other anything else. MateTurnsFailing counts the same runs as error.

panels.title: Session store failures per hour, by op
panels.description: open and rows are mate-db unreachable or slow; migrate is mate retrying its schema at boot; fault a commit that failed mid-turn; quarantine a stored session mate set aside as corrupt. MateStoreFailing fires on more than two in half an hour.

panels.title: Turns and sandboxes, running and waiting
panels.description: Turns running against MATE_MAX_CONCURRENT and the threads queued behind them, and sandboxes leased against MATE_MAX_SANDBOXES and the turns waiting for one. Ten minutes of queue is MateThreadsQueued; fifteen of sandbox waiting is MateSandboxWaitsLong.

panels.title: Reported spend per hour
panels.description: Each run's usage summed at qwen3.8-max's list price from pi's catalog, $2 and $6 per million input and output tokens. The `opencode-go` plan is flat-rate, so this is a shadow of list price, not a bill.

panels.title: Discord identify budget
panels.description: IDENTIFYs left in Discord's rolling day against the fifth of the total mate keeps as a reserve. Read only when mate calls /gateway/bot, and it stops reporting once Discord's own reset window has passed rather than holding a stale number.

panels.title: Gateway closes per hour, by code
panels.description: 4004 and 4010-4014 are configuration errors mate never retries: it counts the close, flushes, and exits. Everything else is a reconnect, and a steady rate of those is what spends the identify budget.
